Lengthen the harder parts over the following weeks
Leave formal intervals until about week 8 or later

joyner-2008.title: Endurance exercise performance: the physiology of champions
joyner-2008.support: For endurance sports three main factors - maximal oxygen consumption (VO2max), the so-called 'lactate threshold' and efficiency (i.e. the oxygen cost to generate a given running speed or cycling power output) - appear to play key roles in endurance performance.

spencer-2001.title: Energy system contribution during 200- to 1500-m running in highly trained athletes
spencer-2001.support: The relative contribution of the aerobic energy system to the 200-, 400-, 800-, and 1500-m events was 29+/-4, 43+/-1, 66+/-2, and 84+/-1%. The crossover to predominantly aerobic energy system supply occurred between 15 and 30 s for the 400-, 800-, and 1500-m events.

seiler-2010.title: What is Best Practice for Training Intensity and Duration Distribution in Endurance Athletes?
seiler-2010.journal: International Journal of Sports Physiology and Performance
seiler-2010.support: Numerous descriptive studies of the training characteristics of nationally or internationally competitive endurance athletes training 10 to 13 times per week seem to converge on a typical intensity distribution in which about 80% of training sessions are performed at low intensity (2 mM blood lactate), with about 20% dominated by periods of high-intensity work.

seiler-2009.title: Intervals, Thresholds, and Long Slow Distance: the Role of Intensity and Duration in Endurance Training
seiler-2009.support: Table 1: a typical five-zone scale (heart rate 55-75, 75-85, 85-90, 90-95, 95-100 %max; lactate 0.8-1.5 up to 6-10 mmol/L). About 80 % of training sessions are performed completely or predominantly at intensities under the first ventilatory turn point, or a blood-lactate concentration of 2 mM or less.

schumacher-2002.title: The 4000-m team pursuit cycling world record: theoretical and practical aspects
schumacher-2002.support: Aerobic performance was trained through high overall training mileage (29,000-35,000 km/yr) with workload peaks during road stage races. Before major track events, anaerobic performance, and track-specific technical and motor skills were improved through discipline-specific track training.

rosenblat-2025.title: Which Training Intensity Distribution Intervention will Produce the Greatest Improvements in Maximal Oxygen Uptake and Time-Trial Performance in Endurance Athletes? A Systematic Review and Network Meta-analysis of Individual Participant Data
rosenblat-2025.support: We included 13 studies with 348 recreational and competitive endurance athletes. There was no difference in VO2max (SMD = -0.06, p = 0.68) or TT performance (SMD = -0.05, p = 0.34) between POL and pyramidal (PYR) interventions. There were no statistically significant differences between POL and any of the other TID interventions.

silva-oliveira-2024.title: Comparison of Polarized Versus Other Types of Endurance Training Intensity Distribution on Athletes’ Endurance Performance: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis
silva-oliveira-2024.support: Seventeen studies met the inclusion criteria (n = 437 subjects). POL is superior to other TIDs for improving VO2peak, particularly in shorter duration interventions and highly trained athletes. However, the effect of POL was similar to that of other TIDs on the remaining surrogates of endurance performance.

robergs-2004.title: Biochemistry of exercise-induced metabolic acidosis
robergs-2004.journal: American Journal of Physiology-Regulatory, Integrative and Comparative Physiology
robergs-2004.support: This review presents clear evidence that there is no biochemical support for lactate production causing acidosis. Lactate production retards, not causes, acidosis. Increased lactate production coincides with cellular acidosis and remains a good indirect marker for cell metabolic conditions that induce metabolic acidosis.

bishop-2011.title: Repeated-Sprint Ability - Part II
bishop-2011.support: Two key recommendations emerge from this review; it is important to include (i) some training to improve single-sprint performance (e.g. 'traditional' sprint training and strength/power training); and (ii) some high-intensity (80-90% maximal oxygen consumption) interval training to best improve the ability to recover between sprints.

bossi-2020.title: Optimizing Interval Training Through Power-Output Variation Within the Work Intervals
bossi-2020.journal: International Journal of Sports Physiology and Performance
bossi-2020.support: Cyclists spent more time at >90% VO2max during HIIT with varied-intensity work intervals (410 [207] vs 286 [162] s, P = .02), but there were no differences between sessions in heart-rate- or perceptual-based training-load metrics.

hickson-1977.title: Linear increase in aerobic power induced by a strenuous program of endurance exercise
hickson-1977.support: Eight subjects exercised for 40 min/day, 6 days/wk for 10 wk. Endurance, VO2max, and time to attainment of peak heart rate all increased linearly during the 10 wk. The total increase in VO2max averaged 16.8 ml/kg per min (44%).

garber-2011.title: Quantity and Quality of Exercise for Developing and Maintaining Cardiorespiratory, Musculoskeletal, and Neuromotor Fitness in Apparently Healthy Adults
garber-2011.support: Educating adults about and screening for signs and symptoms of CHD and gradual progression of exercise intensity and volume may reduce the risks of exercise. Adults who are unable or unwilling to meet the exercise targets outlined here still can benefit from engaging in amounts of exercise less than recommended.

billat-2003.title: The Concept of Maximal Lactate Steady State
billat-2003.support: The maximal lactate steady state (MLSS) is defined as the highest blood lactate concentration (MLSSc) and work load (MLSSw) that can be maintained over time without a continual blood lactate accumulation. MLSSc has been reported to demonstrate a great variability between individuals (from 2-8 mmol/L) in capillary blood and not to be related to MLSSw.

videbaek-2015.title: Incidence of Running-Related Injuries Per 1000 h of running in Different Types of Runners: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
videbaek-2015.support: The meta-analyses revealed a weighted injury incidence of 17.8 (95% CI 16.7-19.1) in novice runners and 7.7 (95% CI 6.9-8.7) in recreational runners per 1000 h of running.

melanson-2002.title: Effect of exercise intensity on 24-h energy expenditure and nutrient oxidation
melanson-2002.support: Both 24-h EE and carbohydrate oxidation were significantly elevated on the exercise days (Con < LI = HI), but 24-h fat oxidation was not different across conditions. It is concluded that exercise intensity has no effect on 24-h EE or nutrient oxidation.

mackey-2021.title: What is known about the FTP20 test related to cycling? A scoping review
mackey-2021.support: Fifteen studies were included. The FTP20 test was reported as a reliable test. Studies investigating the relationship of FTP20 with other physiological markers and power-related concepts reported large limits of agreement suggesting parameters cannot be used interchangeably.

wen-2019.title: Effects of different protocols of high intensity interval training for VO2max improvements in adults: A meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
wen-2019.journal: Journal of Science and Medicine in Sport
wen-2019.support: Fifty-three studies met the eligibility criteria. When compared to MICT, only long-interval (>=2min), high-volume (>=15min) and moderate to long-term (>=4-12weeks) HIIT showed beneficial effects (SMD=0.65-1.07, p<0.05).

mcdonald-endurance-methods-1.title: Methods of Endurance Training Part 1
mcdonald-endurance-methods-1.support: Backs the points that endurance adaptations differ in what triggers them, that no one intensity covers them all, and that a larger aerobic system also helps short hard efforts.

mcdonald-miles-build-champions.title: Methods of Endurance Training Part 2: Miles Build Champions
mcdonald-miles-build-champions.support: Source for the view that high-volume easy training works through sheer volume and frequency, and loses most of its effect when only a few hours a week are available.

mcdonald-tempo-sweet-spot.title: Methods of Endurance Training 3: Tempo and Sweet Spot Training
mcdonald-tempo-sweet-spot.support: Source for the volume-against-intensity trade, the description of tempo and sweet spot work, the small starting dose for beginners and the walk-run start for new runners.

mcdonald-threshold-training.title: Methods of Endurance Training Part 4: Threshold Training
mcdonald-threshold-training.support: Source for how threshold sessions are usually built and limited, for finding threshold from a sustained effort, and for the aerobic-base explanation of acid handling.

mcdonald-interval-training-1.title: Methods of Endurance Training Part 5: Interval Training Part 1
mcdonald-interval-training-1.support: Source for setting interval intensity by pace or power because heart rate lags, for the two-a-week ceiling on hard intervals, and for building a base before adding them.

mcdonald-interval-training-2.title: Methods of Endurance Training Part 5: Interval Training Part 2
mcdonald-interval-training-2.support: Source for the usual structure of VO2 max intervals and strides, and for his view that interval gains level off quickly in trained athletes, so blocks stay short.

mcdonald-endurance-summing-up.title: Methods of Endurance Training: Summing Up Part 1
mcdonald-endurance-summing-up.support: Source for how he fits the methods to recreational racers, team-sport athletes, beginners and dieters, including the interval-block option for people with very few hours.

mcdonald-endurance-predictors.title: Predictors of Endurance Training Performance
mcdonald-endurance-predictors.support: Source for the plain-language account of the three predictors and for the cycling convention of estimating threshold power from a 20-minute effort.

gibala-2012.title: Physiological adaptations to low‐volume, high‐intensity interval training in health and disease
gibala-2012.support: While less well studied, low-volume HIT can also stimulate physiological remodelling comparable to moderate-intensity continuous training despite a substantially lower time commitment and reduced total exercise volume.

milanovic-2015.title: Effectiveness of High-Intensity Interval Training (HIT) and Continuous Endurance Training for VO2max Improvements: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Controlled Trials
milanovic-2015.support: Endurance training and HIT both elicit large improvements in the VO2max of healthy, young to middle-aged adults, with the gains in VO2max being greater following HIT when compared with endurance training (1.2 mL/kg/min, possibly small).

tabata-1996.title: Effects of moderate-intensity endurance and high-intensity intermittent training on anaerobic capacity and ??VO2max
tabata-1996.support: The exhaustive intermittent training consisted of seven to eight sets of 20-s exercise at an intensity of about 170% of VO2max with a 10-s rest between each bout. After the training period, VO2max increased by 7 ml/kg/min, while the anaerobic capacity increased by 28%.

laforgia-2006.title: Effects of exercise intensity and duration on the excess post-exercise oxygen consumption
laforgia-2006.support: Even those studies incorporating exercise stimuli resulting in prolonged EPOC durations have identified that the EPOC comprises only 6-15% of the net total oxygen cost of the exercise. The earlier research optimism regarding an important role for the EPOC in weight loss is generally unfounded.

knab-2011.title: A 45-Minute Vigorous Exercise Bout Increases Metabolic Rate for 14 Hours
knab-2011.support: The 45-min exercise bout resulted in a net energy expenditure of 519 +/- 60.9 kcal. For 14 h after exercise, energy expenditure was increased 190 +/- 71.4 kcal compared with the rest day.

tremblay-1994.title: Impact of exercise intensity on body fatness and skeletal muscle metabolism
tremblay-1994.support: The mean estimated total energy cost of the ET program was 120.4 MJ, whereas the corresponding value for the HIIT program was 57.9 MJ. When corrected for the energy cost of training, the decrease in the sum of six subcutaneous skinfolds induced by the HIIT program was ninefold greater than by the ET program.

gibala-2006.title: Short-term sprint interval versus traditional endurance training: similar initial adaptations in human skeletal muscle and exercise performance
gibala-2006.support: Training time commitment over 2 weeks was approximately 2.5 h for SIT and approximately 10.5 h for ET, and total training volume was approximately 90% lower for SIT versus ET. Training decreased the time required to complete 50 and 750 kJ cycling time trials, with no difference between groups.

panissa-2021.title: Magnitude and duration of excess of post‐exercise oxygen consumption between high‐intensity interval and moderate‐intensity continuous exercise: A systematic review
panissa-2021.support: Twenty-two studies were included in the final evaluation. The long-duration evaluations resulted in greater EPOC for HIIE (average of ~289 kJ) compared with MICE (average of ~159 kJ). Most short-duration evaluations that subtracted baseline EE reported higher EPOC for HIIE (average of ~136 kJ) compared with MICE (average of ~101 kJ).

steele-2021.title: Slow and Steady, or Hard and Fast? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Studies Comparing Body Composition Changes between Interval Training and Moderate Intensity Continuous Training
steele-2021.support: The main model for fat mass effects revealed a trivial standardized point estimate with high precision for the interval estimate (-0.016 (95%CI -0.07 to 0.04)). The main model for fat-free mass effects revealed a trivial standardized point estimate (-0.0004 (95%CI -0.05 to 0.05)). The GRADE summary of findings suggested high certainty for both main model effects.

wewege-2017.title: The effects of high‐intensity interval training vs. moderate‐intensity continuous training on body composition in overweight and obese adults: a systematic review and meta‐analysis
wewege-2017.support: From 1,334 articles initially screened, 13 were included. There were no significant differences between HIIT and MICT for any body composition measure, but HIIT required ~40% less training time commitment.

lindner-2023.title:
Moderate to Vigorous-intensity Continuous Training versus Highintensity
                    Interval Training for Improving VO2max in Women: A
                    Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
lindner-2023.support: There was no statistical difference in VO2max improvements after training between women in the MVICT and HIIT cohorts (mean difference: -0.42, 95%CI: -1.43 to 0.60, p>0.05). Long-HIIT was superior to short-HIIT protocols at increasing VO2max.

mcdonald-interval-adaptations.title: Metabolic Adaptations to Interval Training
mcdonald-interval-adaptations.support: Source for the cautions on sprint-interval research: untrained subjects, all-out efforts on a special bike, short follow-up, and little likeness to gym interval classes.

mcdonald-tabata.title: Effects of Moderate- and High-Intensity Intermitten Training
mcdonald-tabata.support: Source for the argument that the Tabata result belongs to its very high work rate on a bike, and that timer-based circuits sharing the name are a different thing.

mcdonald-steady-state-hiit-1.title: Steady State and Interval Training: Part 1
mcdonald-steady-state-hiit-1.support: Source for his costs and benefits of steady versus interval cardio, the break-in for beginners, cutting leg lifting to fit intervals, and same-day sequencing.

mcdonald-steady-state-summary.title: Steady State vs. Interval Training: Summing Up Part 1
mcdonald-steady-state-summary.support: Source for the point that interval studies test people who are not lifting or dieting, and for his rule that carbohydrate intake and high-intensity volume must fit each other.

mcdonald-hiit-disconnect.title: Steady state vs. Interval Intervals: Explaining the Disconnect
mcdonald-hiit-disconnect.support: Source for his explanations of why uncontrolled trials sometimes favoured intervals for fat loss: appetite, effort level and small absolute changes.

mcdonald-epoc-application.title: Steady State vs. Interval Training and EPOC
mcdonald-epoc-application.support: Source for the argument that a larger afterburn percentage on a short interval session still totals less than a longer steady session burns.

mcdonald-epoc-review.title: Excess Post-exercise Oxygen Consumption
mcdonald-epoc-review.support: His walk through the 2006 EPOC review, concluding that energy burned during the session matters far more than the afterburn.

mcdonald-epoc-45-minutes.title: The Increase in Metabolic Rate from a 45 Minute Workout
mcdonald-epoc-45-minutes.support: Source for the cautions on the chamber study: subjects were fed to energy balance, the ride was very hard, and an easier, longer ride burns a similar total.

schoenfeld-2014.title: Body composition changes associated with fasted versus non-fasted aerobic exercise
schoenfeld-2014.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
schoenfeld-2014.support: Twenty healthy young female volunteers were randomly assigned to 1 of 2 experimental groups. Training consisted of 1 hour of steady-state aerobic exercise performed 3 days per week. Both groups showed a significant loss of weight (P = 0.0005) and fat mass (P = 0.02) from baseline, but no significant between-group differences were noted in any outcome measure.

hackett-2017.title: Effect of Overnight Fasted Exercise on Weight Loss and Body Composition: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
hackett-2017.journal: Journal of Functional Morphology and Kinesiology
hackett-2017.support: A total of five studies were included involving 96 participants. The inter-group effect for the interventions on body mass was trivial.

vieira-2016.title: Effects of aerobic exercise performed in fasted v. fed state on fat and carbohydrate metabolism in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis
vieira-2016.support: Of 10 405 articles identified, twenty-seven studies - with a total of 273 participants - were included. We conclude that aerobic exercise performed in the fasted state induces higher fat oxidation than exercise performed in the fed state.

bellicha-2021.title: Effect of exercise training on weight loss, body composition changes, and weight maintenance in adults with overweight or obesity: An overview of 12 systematic reviews and 149 studies
bellicha-2021.support: Overview of 12 systematic reviews (149 studies); exercise led to weight loss of 1.5-3.5 kg; resistance training reduced lean mass loss during weight loss; no difference between aerobic and HIIT when energy expenditure is equal.

wing-2005.title: Long-term weight loss maintenance
wing-2005.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
wing-2005.support: Members have lost an average of 33 kg and maintained the loss for more than 5 y, with about 1 h/d of physical activity, self-monitoring of weight and a consistent eating pattern across weekdays and weekends.

odriscoll-2020.title: How well do activity monitors estimate energy expenditure? A systematic review and meta-analysis of the validity of current technologies
odriscoll-2020.support: 60 studies (104 effect sizes); devices showed variable accuracy depending on activity type, with large heterogeneity.

lemon-1980.title: Effect of initial muscle glycogen levels on protein catabolism during exercise
lemon-1980.support: Six subjects (27-30 yr) pedaled a cycle ergometer for 1 h at 61% VO2max 1) after CHO loading and 2) after CHO depletion. Calculations indicate that CHOD sweat urea N excretion was equivalent to a protein breakdown of 13.7 g/h or 10.4% of the total caloric cost.

hopker-2009.title: The Effects of Training on Gross Efficiency in Cycling: A Review
hopker-2009.support: We present an overview of these studies and their relative shortcomings and conclude that in well-controlled and rigorously designed studies, training has a positive influence upon gross efficiency.

mcdonald-fasted-cardio-1.title: Is Fasted Cardio Useless for Fat Loss?
mcdonald-fasted-cardio-1.support: Source for the three-step account of fat loss, for which step limits lean versus obese dieters, and for what an overnight fast does and does not change.

mcdonald-fasted-cardio-2.title: Is Fasted Cardio Useless for Fat Loss: Part 2
mcdonald-fasted-cardio-2.support: Source for his critique of applying the one diet-controlled trial to very lean dieters, and for his view that protein use during cardio is too small to threaten muscle.

mcdonald-fasted-cardio-qa.title: Fasted Cardio and Fat Loss - Q&A
mcdonald-fasted-cardio-qa.support: Short statement of his position: timing of cardio matters only, if at all, for lean people getting leaner; everyone else should do it when it gets done.

mcdonald-exercise-efficiency.title: Exercise Efficiency
mcdonald-exercise-efficiency.support: Source for the reply to the claim that steady cardio stops working: efficiency moves only a little, over years, and workload can simply be raised.

mcdonald-exercise-weight-loss.title: Exercise and Weight/Fat Loss: Part 1
mcdonald-exercise-weight-loss.support: Source for his working figures on energy burned per minute, the small deficit from realistic exercise, overestimated burns, and the larger role in keeping weight off.

schumann-2022.title: Compatibility of Concurrent Aerobic and Strength Training for Skeletal Muscle Size and Function: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
schumann-2022.support: A total of 43 studies were included. Concurrent aerobic and strength training does not compromise muscle hypertrophy and maximal strength development.

lundberg-2022.title: The Effects of Concurrent Aerobic and Strength Training on Muscle Fiber Hypertrophy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
lundberg-2022.support: A total of 15 studies were included. In contrast to previous findings on whole muscle hypertrophy, the present results suggest that concurrent aerobic and strength training may have a small negative effect on fiber hypertrophy compared with strength training alone.

sabag-2018.title: The compatibility of concurrent high intensity interval training and resistance training for muscular strength and hypertrophy: a systematic review and meta-analysis
sabag-2018.support: Compared to RT alone, concurrent HIIT and RT led to similar changes in muscle hypertrophy and upper body strength. Concurrent HIIT and RT resulted in a lower increase in lower body strength compared to RT alone (ES = -0.248, p = 0.049).

wilson-2012.title: Concurrent Training
wilson-2012.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
wilson-2012.support: A meta-analysis of 21 studies was performed with a total of 422 effect sizes. The mean ES for hypertrophy for strength training was 1.23; for endurance training, it was 0.27; and for concurrent training, it was 0.85. Resistance training concurrently with running, but not cycling, resulted in significant decrements in both hypertrophy and strength.

spiering-2021.title: Maintaining Physical Performance: The Minimal Dose of Exercise Needed to Preserve Endurance and Strength Over Time
spiering-2021.support: Endurance performance can be maintained for up to 15 weeks when training frequency is reduced to as little as 2 sessions per week or when exercise volume is reduced by 33-66%, as long as exercise intensity is maintained. Strength and muscle size (at least in younger populations) can be maintained for up to 32 weeks with as little as 1 session of strength training per week and 1 set per exercise, as long as exercise intensity (relative load) is maintained.

haugen-2019.title: The Training and Development of Elite Sprint Performance: an Integration of Scientific and Best Practice Literature
haugen-2019.support: Such training is typified by runs lasting 7-15 s at 95-100% intensity, with full recovery used between repetitions and sets. A rule of thumb among practitioners is that 1-2-min recovery is required for every second spent on maximal sprinting.

mcdonald-sprint-training.title: What is Sprint Training?
mcdonald-sprint-training.support: Source for the distinction between gym intervals and real sprint work: very short maximal efforts, long passive rests, long warm-ups, hours per session and little energy burned.

mcdonald-sprinter-vs-endurance.title: The Sprinter Versus Endurance Athlete...Again
mcdonald-sprinter-vs-endurance.support: Source for the argument that athletes' builds reflect selection and weight training, so the kind of cardio you do will not give you a sprinter's physique.

mcdonald-indoor-aerobic.title: Surviving Indoor Aerobic Training
mcdonald-indoor-aerobic.support: Source for dividing indoor sessions into blocks with a change at each boundary, timed pick-ups, alternating machine levels to progress, and stepped sessions.

mcdonald-sports-continuum.title: The Sports Training and Adaptation Continuum
mcdonald-sports-continuum.support: Source for his three-part continuum of sports, from strength and power through mixed sports to endurance, and how it sets training and adaptations.

mcdonald-cardio-mass-gains.title: Cardio and Mass Gains
mcdonald-cardio-mass-gains.support: Source for his case for small amounts of easy, low-impact cardio while gaining, its dose and timing limits, and the exception for naturally thin lifters.

mcdonald-weights-marathon.title: Combining Weight Training with Marathon/Century Training
mcdonald-weights-marathon.support: Source for cutting lifting to brief maintenance sessions during an endurance build-up and for placing them so the long session is never done on tired legs.

ekkekakis-2011.title: The Pleasure and Displeasure People Feel When they Exercise at Different Intensities
ekkekakis-2011.support: This review examines 33 articles published from 1999 to 2009 on the relationship between exercise intensity and affective responses. There are pleasant changes at sub-threshold intensities for most individuals, large inter-individual variability close to the ventilatory or lactate threshold and homogeneously negative changes at supra-threshold intensities. When the intensity is self-selected, rather than imposed, it appears to foster greater tolerance to higher intensity levels.

williams-2008.title: Exercise, Affect, and Adherence: An Integrated Model and a Case for Self-Paced Exercise
williams-2008.journal: Journal of Sport and Exercise Psychology
williams-2008.support: Affective response to exercise is posited to influence exercise adherence via anticipated affective response to future exercise. Further evidence in support of self-paced exercise could have implications for exercise prescription, especially among overweight, sedentary adults, who are most in need of interventions that enhance adherence to exercise programs.

murphy-2019.title: The Effects of Continuous Compared to Accumulated Exercise on Health: A Meta-Analytic Review
murphy-2019.support: A total of 19 studies involving 1080 participants met the inclusion criteria. There were no differences between accumulated and continuous groups for any cardiorespiratory fitness or blood pressure outcomes. A difference was found in body mass changes from baseline to post-intervention in favour of accumulated exercise compared with continuous (MD -0.92 kg, 95% CI -1.59 to -0.25; five studies, 211 participants).

wang-2010.title: Specific metabolic rates of major organs and tissues across adulthood: evaluation by mechanistic model of resting energy expenditure
wang-2010.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
wang-2010.support: The specific resting metabolic rates (in kcal/kg/d) of major organs and tissues in adults were suggested by Elia to be as follows: 13 for skeletal muscle, 4.5 for adipose tissue. Elia's Ki values were within the range of 95% CIs in the young and middle-age groups.

mcdonald-obese-beginner-1.title: Training the Obese Beginner
mcdonald-obese-beginner-1.support: Background for the term metabolic flexibility: his account of why people with obesity and inactivity often burn relatively less fat, and that activity improves this.

mcdonald-obese-beginner-2.title: Training the Obese Beginner: Part 2
mcdonald-obese-beginner-2.support: Source for the point that added muscle changes resting energy use very little, that lean mass rises with obesity, and that lifting should not crowd out other activity.

mcdonald-obese-beginner-3.title: Training the Obese Beginner: Part 3
mcdonald-obese-beginner-3.support: Source for using simple, higher-repetition strength work and gradually rising cardio to restore the use of fat as fuel, starting from a low volume.

mcdonald-obese-beginner-4.title: Training the Obese Beginner: Part 4
mcdonald-obese-beginner-4.support: Source for putting consistency first, for the damage done by a punishing first session, and for self-paced effort below threshold in reluctant beginners.

mcdonald-obese-beginner-5.title: Training the Obese Beginner: Part 5
mcdonald-obese-beginner-5.support: Source for doing strength work and cardio from day one, a short first session, splitting cardio into bouts, and skipping skinfolds and maximum tests at intake.

mcdonald-obese-beginner-6.title: Training the Obese Beginner: Part 6
mcdonald-obese-beginner-6.support: Source for the first-session walking routine, effort of 3 to 4 out of 10, the 20-minute target, small weekly progressions, machine-first strength work and delaying intervals.
